item.title: Proinflammatory strains of Mediterraneibacter gnavus are enriched during spondyloarthritis and bolster disease severity in animal model.
item.author: Jacoutot M, Munhoz DD, Beaufrère M, Boukamel A, Gautreau G, Bergot AS, Said-Nahal R, Robert V, Karpman P, Frison E, Cai B, Ouahbi D, Lamarque D, Bazin T, Manuello T, Dumas E, Maraquin P, Rizzo LV, Chatel JM, Langella P, Elewaut D, Thomas R, Breban M, Glatigny S.
item.description:
Spondyloarthritis (SpA) is a chronic inflammatory rheumatism with osteoarticular and extra‑articular manifestations. Intestinal dysbiosis has been implicated in SpA, notably the expansion of Mediterraneibacter gnavus (MG), a gram-positive coccus associated with several inflammatory disorders. We aimed to determine whether distinct MG strains were associated with SpA and contributed to disease pathogenesis. MG strains from patients with SpA and healthy controls (HCs) were identified based on metagenomic analysis, isolated and whole‑genome sequenced. Pathogenicity of selected strains was compared by mono-associating curdlan-treated germ‑free SpA-prone SKG mice. Putative strain selection under inflammatory pressure was examined by culturing MG in the presence of nitric oxide (NO). item.title: Spatial transcriptomics in immune-mediated necrotising myopathy uncovers a specific necrotic signature related to immune-driven fibrosis.
item.author: Dal Cin J, Mahoudeau A, N'Diaye D, Bensalah M, Muraine L, Tendrel B, Anquetil C, Amelin D, Bolko L, Chenane L, Letourneur F, Madelaine A, Léonard-Louis S, Negroni E, Trollet C, Benveniste O, Allenbach Y.
item.description:
Immune-mediated necrotising myopathies (IMNM) are characterised by muscle fibre necrosis, complement deposits around non-necrotic fibres, and macrophage infiltrates. Patients experience muscle damage with fibro-fatty replacement, leading to poor strength recovery, but the pathogenesis remains unclear. To investigate IMNM pathogenesis, we applied spatial transcriptomics on myositis muscle biopsies and integrated the results with published single-nucleus transcriptomic data. This combined approach enabled analysis of gene expression with spatial localisation in the muscle. Inflammatory, fibrotic, regenerative, and lipid metabolism-related signatures were identified in IMNM, distinct from other myositis, with specific distribution in necrotic and peri-necrotic regions. item.author: Eming SA, Kreuter A, Hahn M, Ghoreschi K, Moinzadeh P, Hunzelmann N, Becker K, Reiche N, Adams A, Shah-Hosseini K, Hellmich M, Willenborg S, Sanin DE, Röcken M, Krieg T.
item.description:
Objectives Fibrotic diseases are a major therapeutic challenge. In humans, fibrosing diseases are often associated with an interleukin (IL-) 4/T H 2 signature. In preclinical mouse models, development of fibrosis critically depends on IL-4/signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6). Yet, the role of IL-4/IL-13 in human fibrosing diseases remains unknown, and treatment development requires a deeper understanding of the role of IL-4/IL-13 in the pathogenesis. The local inflammation and the development of fibrosis in localised scleroderma (LS) are similar to those in systemic sclerosis and other fibrosing diseases. item.title: Practical recommendations for revaccination following BCMA-targeted therapies in adult patients with autoimmune diseases.
item.author: Winthrop KL, Calabrese L, Bingham C, Mariette X, Zhou C, Mozaffarian N.
item.description:
Objectives B-cell-directed immune-reset therapies are emerging as transformative approaches in autoimmune diseases, but their impact on long-term humoral immunity remains uncertain. These strategies encompass a broad range of B-cell targets and therapeutic modalities, the most clinically established targets include CD19, CD20, and B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA), with T-cell-redirecting approaches, particularly chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies and bispecific T-cell engagers, among the most validated modalities. Here, we aim to provide a practical framework for revaccination in patients with autoimmune diseases. Methods We examine existing clinical evidence on the effects of BCMA-targeting therapies with respect to antivaccine titres to provide a revaccination framework in autoimmunity. Objectives To evaluate 6-month effectiveness and long-term drug-retention rates of biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs) in psoriatic arthritis (PsA) using real-world data analysed within an emulated multicentre clinical trial framework. Secondary objectives included the characterisation of response profiles and the identification of possible predictors of clinical response across bDMARD classes. item.author: Bond M, Hysa E, Konzett V, van der Geest KSM, Sattui SE, Amudala N, Fruth M, Gheysens O, Helliwell T, Josten C, Keller KK, Kermani TA, Kohler MJ, Liew DFL, Mackie SL, Magri SJ, Michailidou D, Neill L, Owen CE, Putman M, Schmidt WA, Slart RHJA, de Souza AWS, Sugihara T, Tiwari V, Toonder B, Unizony S, Warrington KJ, Ramiro S, Dejaco C.
item.description:
Objectives The study aims to develop international recommendations for the use of imaging in the diagnosis and assessment of polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR). Methods An international, multidisciplinary task force of 30 members from 12 countries was convened; the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology standard operating procedures were followed. Six clinical key questions addressing the role of imaging (ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging, and 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography) in diagnosis, monitoring, outcome prediction, and technical aspects in PMR were the basis for a systematic literature review. Recommendations were formulated based on evidence and expert opinion and refined iteratively until consensus was achieved. The level of agreement was assessed by voting.
